doc.name: The Sixth World after October 2059 (GM only)

text.content:
New Seattle gives no year for these two changes. It reports them in posts dated 2060. They follow O'Malley's death on New Year's Day 2058 (NS p.97), so place them where your campaign needs them.

The Mafia: Bigio becomes capo

After O'Malley's death, his daughter Rowena took the Finnigan Family and the families fought for control. The Commissione put Don Leo McCaskill of Milwaukee in charge of the situation. When the dust settled, on McCaskill's advice it appointed Maurice "Butcher" Bigio capo of Seattle (NS p.97). Vince Ciarniello sided with Bigio (NS p.100); Rowena O'Malley, with "Uncle Al" Cavalieri behind her, may yet challenge him (NS p.100).

The yakuza break with Japan

Hanzo Shotozumi declared the Seattle yakuza independent of the Watada-rengo in Japan, as the Shotozumi-rengo. Akira Watada and the loyalist clans in California are angered, and a new shadow war is expected, though there have been no reprisals yet (NS p.101). His wakagashira-hosa, Miko Ishikawa, spies for the Watada-rengo (NS p.101).

  • Mitsuhama loses the yakuza help it relied on and hires more shadowrunners instead (NS p.92–93).
  • Japan loses shadow assets in Seattle, and a yakuza civil war is possible (NS p.81).
  • Runners predict a temporary Triad–Shotozumi alliance against Mitsuhama and the Japan-loyal yakuza (NS p.96).

GM only. This compendium is hidden from players. The public guide's World pages describe the Sixth World as of October 2059. Everything here happens after that, as the SR3 core book (set in 2060) and New Seattle (posts dated 2060) describe it.

Reveal it when your campaign reaches it, or change it: it's your world.

Hidden, not secret: players don't see this compendium in Foundry, but the system is public, so a determined player could find it in the system's files or from the browser console.

Where a book gives only a year, this journal says so. The core book's history and New Seattle's Shadowland posts are in-character sources: treat "runners claim" as rumour.

2060: Fuchi is dissolved

By October 2059, Richard Villiers has already formed Novatech and is quietly buying his Fuchi North America holdings into it (SR3 p.35). In 2060 the corp war claimed Fuchi: Villiers took his part to Novatech, and the other two factions bought and married into Renraku and Shiawase, which absorbed the rest until Fuchi was officially dissolved (SR3 p.35). The core book's narrator says the Big Eight have become "the Big-No-One-Knows-How-Many" (SR3 p.35).

  • The Court hasn't ruled on Fuchi's subsidiaries: Novatech, Renraku and Shiawase all claim them, and each works to make its claim the strongest (NS p.95).
  • Renraku survives on its alliance with the Nakatomi family's part of Fuchi (NS p.94).
  • Shiawase moves into cyberware with former Fuchi assets (NS p.95–96).
  • Pacific Rim Communications buys up the telecomm contracts Fuchi lost (NS p.87).

Novatech in Seattle

  • Villiers's ex-wife Samantha Villiers runs Novatech Seattle from the former Fuchi compound downtown, stripped of every Fuchi logo (NS p.93–94).
  • William Ager, Fuchi's old "resources adjuster", now runs Novatech's black ops in Seattle and hires runners as needed (NS p.94).
  • The shadow war between Novatech downtown and Renraku in Bellevue has already begun (NS p.94).

2060: Cross takes Renraku's seat

After Renraku's representative died in the New Delhi bombing, Cross Applied Technologies was given Renraku's seat on the Corporate Court, which the core book says must have made Damien Knight furious (SR3 p.35). (Wuxing had already taken Fuchi's seat in 2059.)

December 2059: the arcology goes dark

On an evening just before Christmas 2059, the Renraku Arcology's systems went off-line, and Renraku sealed it from the public with no comment (SR3 p.35; NS p.30). The UCAS military had stepped in by January 2060 (SR3 p.35). More than 100,000 people were sealed inside, among them Governor Schultz, who had gone there for a meeting. Charles Lindstrom took charge of the metroplex and promised to protect those trapped; runners doubt he wants her back (NS p.30, p.76).

Joint Task Force Seattle

  • The UCAS sent Joint Task Force Seattle: five thousand soldiers and airmen under Brigadier General Angela Colloton (NS p.78).
  • Humanis recruits from the Metroplex Guard, and some Guard officers hold Humanis posts. After Guardsmen were arrested for racially motivated attacks on metahuman soldiers, Colloton purged officers from the Guard. Both the Guard and Humanis now look for ways to get her removed (NS p.78).
  • The extra UCAS troops revived old hostilities with the NAN and the Salish-Shidhe (NS p.81).

Renraku afterwards

  • Renraku's president, Inazo Aneki, is on indefinite leave. Tadashi Marushige, a troubleshooter with a reputation for making heads roll, is acting director of Renraku North America (NS p.94).
  • Renraku Seattle works from a new compound in Bellevue. Its once laid-back security is now aggressive, and its Matrix security "double-ultra-paranoid", with cascading black ice (NS p.94).
  • In 2060 Renraku's Corporate Court representative was killed in a terrorist bombing in New Delhi (SR3 p.35); see Fuchi, Novatech and the Court.
